stories.title: Flexday Opens Flexible Office Space in Chicago’s Loop
stories.excerpt: JLL announced that Flexday, a national provider of flexible office solutions, has launched four fractional office suites at PNC Centre at One North Franklin in the heart of Chicago’s Loop. The suites total more than 25,000 square feet and are designed to accommodate teams of 10 to 70 with flexible, on-demand, and recurring terms, giving companies access to a Class A address and environment without a lease commitment.The launch was made possible through a partnership with MetLife Investment Management, the building’s ownership group, as part of a broader capital investment in PNC Centre that includes a newly renovated lobby and upgraded tenant amenities. JLL leasing brokers, Brad Despot, Senior Managing Director and Kim Doyle, Senior Vice President, along with Catherine Walsh, Vice President and General Manager at JLL represent MetLife Investment Management at PNC Centre. The post Flexday Opens Flexible Office Space in Chicago’s Loop appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Flexday launches 25,000 SF flexible office at PNC Centre, Chicago Loop
MetLife Investment Management backing; renovated lobby and upgraded amenities
Targets 10–70 person teams with no long-term lease commitment
stories.summary: Flexday and MetLife have opened 25,000 SF of fractional office suites at PNC Centre in Chicago's Loop, designed for teams of 10–70 seeking flexible, commitment-free occupancy. The launch is part of a broader capital investment by MetLife in the building that includes lobby renovation and tenant amenity upgrades. This flexible office model competes directly with traditional office leasing.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Flexible office growth signals continued corporate tenant uncertainty and reduced demand for long-term, large-footprint leases—not a demand driver for apartments. Relevant only if it indicates Chicago Loop office weakness offsetting residential demand near employment centers.

stories.title: Colliers Represents ClarkDietrich in Anchor Lease at Ohio Office Development
stories.excerpt: Colliers represented ClarkDietrich in a 32,558-square-foot office lease that will occupy nearly three-quarters of a new office building at Montgomery Quarter, a mixed-use development located at 9260 Montgomery Road in Cincinnati, Ohio. John Schenk, senior vice president, and Matt Smyth, vice president, with Colliers | Cincinnati represented the tenant throughout the site selection and lease negotiation process. “This transaction demonstrates that well-located, high-quality office space continues to attract tenants making long-term commitments in the Cincinnati market,” said Schenk. Located along the Montgomery Road corridor in Cincinnati’s northeastern suburbs, ClarkDietrich’s new office provides access to a mix of retail and dining amenities, structured parking and a modern workplace environment designed to support employee collaboration. ClarkDietrich, a manufacturer of cold-formed steel framing products and systems, plans to relocate approximately 90 employees to the new office. The company is expected to occupy the space in October 2027. The post Colliers Represents ClarkDietrich in Anchor Lease at Ohio Office Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ClarkDietrich leases 32,558 SF at Montgomery Quarter, Cincinnati suburbs, Oct 2027 occupancy
90-employee relocation to Montgomery Road corridor in northeastern Cincinnati
Anchor tenant demonstrates office market strength in well-located suburban Cincinnati
stories.summary: ClarkDietrich, a cold-formed steel framing manufacturer, has leased 32,558 SF (75% of the new building) at Montgomery Quarter mixed-use development on Montgomery Road in Cincinnati's northeastern suburbs. The company plans to relocate 90 employees to the space in October 2027. The transaction signals sustained corporate demand for Class A suburban office with retail and dining nearby.
stories.impact: Modest positive signal for Cincinnati-area multifamily: ClarkDietrich's 90-person relocation to the northeast suburbs corridor will drive localized housing demand in that submarket. Developers should track Montgomery Road and nearby submarkets for apartment site acquisition and pipeline development ahead of 2027 occupancy.

stories.title: Apartment Property in Downtown Wenatche Changes Hands
stories.excerpt: Tamarack, a 23-unit apartment community at 211 N. Delaware Avenue in Wenatchee, Washington, has sold for $3.25 million. Kidder Mathews Vice President Max Frame of the Simon | Anderson Multifamily Team represented the seller, Dan Dahl. The 21,400-square-foot garden-style community is located steps from downtown Wenatchee and offers investors a value-add opportunity in a highly competitive multifamily market. Tamarack went under contract just three days after being listed and sold for approximately $141,304 per unit. The sale marks the property’s first change of ownership in 19 years. “The speed at which Tamarack went under contract reflects the strong demand we continue to see for well-located multifamily opportunities in Wenatchee,” said Frame. “The property had been thoughtfully maintained over many years, giving buyers a strong existing asset with additional upside. Combined with its location near downtown, that made it a compelling opportunity and generated immediate interest.” The post Apartment Property in Downtown Wenatche Changes Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tamarack, 23-unit garden-style apartment, Wenatchee downtown sold $3.25M ($141.3K/unit)
First ownership change in 19 years; listed and under contract in 3 days
Value-add opportunity in tight, competitive Wenatchee multifamily market
stories.summary: Tamarack, a 23-unit garden-style apartment community in downtown Wenatchee, sold for $3.25 million ($141,304/unit) after going under contract in just three days—its first ownership change in 19 years. The property's thoughtful maintenance and downtown location made it an immediate draw for buyers, reflecting strong investor appetite for well-located Wenatchee multifamily assets.
stories.impact: Wenatchee multifamily market is heating up: rapid sale velocity and value-add buyer interest signal rising cap rates, tight supply, and sustained demand. For Trammell Crow, this indicates a window to acquire land or redevelopment sites in downtown Wenatchee before cap rates tighten further; supply constraints and buyer competition will only intensify.

stories.title: Alterra IOS Expands Baltimore-Area Footprint with Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Alterra IOS continues to grow its Baltimore-area footprint with the acquisition of a new, fully leased industrial property at 9729 Philadelphia Road in Rosedale, Maryland. The site features 4.7 usable acres and 22,500 square feet of building improvements in close proximity to I-95 and I-695. The transaction represents Alterra’s seventh acquisition in the Baltimore MSA. Andrew Meeder of MacKenzie Companies assisted in the transaction. The property sits in Rosedale, positioning it along a key freight corridor connecting Baltimore with Philadelphia, New York and the broader Northeast. The deal brings Alterra’s Baltimore-area portfolio to a total of seven acquisitions. Baltimore continues to be an attractive market for Alterra, given its tight supply of IOS properties with a vacancy rate of about 2.5%, strong demand from logistics and transportation users, and proximity to the Port of Baltimore. The post Alterra IOS Expands Baltimore-Area Footprint with Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alterra IOS acquires fully leased industrial, 22,500 SF, Rosedale, Maryland (7th Baltimore deal)
4.7 acres near I-95 and I-695; tight 2.5% vacancy in Baltimore IOS market
Strategic position along Northeast freight corridor (Baltimore–Philadelphia–NYC)
stories.summary: Alterra IOS acquired a fully leased 22,500 SF industrial property on 4.7 acres in Rosedale, Maryland near I-95 and I-695—its seventh acquisition in the Baltimore MSA. The Baltimore area offers attractive fundamentals: approximately 2.5% vacancy, strong logistics and transportation demand, and proximity to the Port of Baltimore and the Northeast corridor.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. Industrial absorption and logistics growth in Baltimore do signal job and population in-migration to the region, which over time boosts apartment demand. However, this news focuses on industrial/IOS supply, not housing. Monitor if logistics expansion drives wage growth and household formation in Baltimore suburbs; that would strengthen multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: Merchants Capital Secures $98M for VA Affordable Development
stories.excerpt: Leading financial services provider Merchants Capital announced $97.8 million in financing for the rehabilitation of Stuart Gardens, a 491-unit, two-phased affordable multifamily property in Newport News, Virginia. developed by Vitus Group. Merchants Capital secured $62.8 million in U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) 221(d)(4) permanent financing and $35 million in equity bridge loans provided by Merchants Bank. Stuart Gardens’ capital stack also includes low-income housing tax credit and green and resilient retrofit program financing via HUD for energy-efficient improvements. Stuart Gardens comprises 109 two-story buildings, with 489 of 491 units across both properties, 100% of the residential units, restricted to families earning 60% area median income. Constructed in 1940, it has been designated as a historic property by the Virginia Board of Historic Resources. Upon completion, Stuart Gardens will offer updated one, two and three-bedroom apartments. Located in a mixed-use neighborhood southeast of downtown Newport News, Stuart Gardens sits within a 1.5-mile radius of schools, public transportation, recreation areas, fire and police stations and grocery stores. The post Merchants Capital Secures $98M for VA Affordable Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Merchants Capital secures $97.8M for Stuart Gardens, 491-unit affordable rehab, Newport News, VA
$62.8M HUD 221(d)(4) permanent + $35M equity bridge; LIHTC and green retrofit funding
Historic 1940 property; units capped at 60% AMI; completion creates modern 1–3BR stock
stories.summary: Merchants Capital closed $97.8 million in financing for Stuart Gardens, a 491-unit affordable multifamily rehabilitation in Newport News, Virginia. The capital stack includes $62.8M in HUD 221(d)(4) permanent financing, $35M in equity bridge loans, plus LIHTC and HUD green/resilient retrofit grants. All 489 residential units are restricted to families earning 60% AMI and will be updated with modern one, two, and three-bedroom units.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to market-rate multifamily development. However, the deal signals strong HUD 221(d)(4) and LIHTC availability in the Hampton Roads/Newport News area, indicating government support for affordable housing. For Trammell Crow, this suggests regulatory appetite for density and mixed-income development in the region; consider policy environment favorable for market-rate+affordable mixed-income projects in Newport News/Hampton Roads.

stories.title: Charter School Inks 56K-SF Lease in Retail Center Near Miami Suburb
stories.excerpt: Charter school network BridgePrep Academy will open another location, this time inside a shopping center in Miami-Dade County. The school operator, which has 19 locations across Florida, signed a 56,000-square-foot lease at the open-air California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, near Aventura, 15 miles north of Downtown Miami. The 273,050-square-foot property, owned by RK Centers, sits west of Interstate 95 at 750 Ives Dairy Road. Other tenants at California Club include Planet Fitness, Five Below and Burlington. Waterways Preparatory Academy @ Kropp Annex, part of the public Dade County School District, previously leased BridgePrep’s new space up until at least last year. “Miami doesn’t have a surplus of properties that work for educational operators,” CBRE’s Scott Goldstein, who represented the tenant alongside Keith Edelman, said in a statement. “We moved quickly.” Some of the challenges include the lack of available properties that have the correct code and layout. Demand for grade schools, mostly for private ones, has skyrocketed in South Florida since the onset of the pandemic, when a slew of new-market companies opened offices and their employees moved in tow. To fix the issue, billionaire developer Stephen Ross is donating $100 million to Pine Crest School, a private school with locations in Fort Lauderdale and Boca Raton, to open another in West Palm Beach, Bloomberg reported. Another billionaire, Jeff Greene, has spent $50 million to build The Greene School, also in West Palm Beach, the Wall Street Journal reported. BridgePrep Academy and RK Centers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgePrep Academy signs 56,000 SF lease at California Club Shopping Center, Ives Estates, Miami-Dade
Charter school has 19 Florida locations; demand for private schools surged post-pandemic in South Florida
Shopping center 15 miles north of Downtown Miami; tenant mix includes Planet Fitness, Five Below, Burlington
stories.summary: BridgePrep Academy, a charter school network with 19 Florida locations, has leased 56,000 SF at California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, Miami-Dade County (15 miles north of Downtown Miami). The lease reflects surging demand for private and charter school space in South Florida since the pandemic, with brokers noting scarcity of available properties with correct code and layout for educational operators.
stories.impact: Indirect multifamily demand signal for South Florida: charter school expansion and post-pandemic migration to private education indicate sustained household in-migration and family formation in Miami-Dade, particularly in northern/suburban areas (Ives Estates, near Aventura). Developers should track charter/private school openings as leading indicators of family demographic density; these areas warrant multifamily acquisition and pipeline development targeting 2–3 bedroom, family-oriented units.

stories.title: Taco Bell’s Office Lease Largest in Orange County, Calif., in Five Years
stories.excerpt: Orange County, Calif.’s office market improved again in the third quarter thanks to a diverse set of corporate leases. Total vacancy improved to 15.4 percent, down from 17.1 percent a year ago, while average asking rents increased to $3.02 per square foot per month, up from $2.90 at the end of 2025, according to new data from JLL. Net absorption slipped slightly for the quarter, but remained positive on the year at 265,394 square feet, compared to negative 158,099 square feet for all of 2025. Tenants signed about 1.55 million square feet of leases during the quarter, led by Taco Bell’s 254,162-square-foot lease at Irvine Company’s Alton HQ, the largest office lease signed in Orange County in five years. (The maker of the Crunchwrap Supreme plans to relocate from its current Irvine headquarters in 2028.) Medical device maker Envista Holdings also signed for 101,800 square feet across three buildings, while an unnamed aerospace company took 173,057 square feet across two Airport Area properties, including 102,417 square feet at 4000 MacArthur Boulevard. The South County submarket posted the strongest quarterly absorption at 86,107 square feet, with Irvine Company’s Irvine Spectrum campus contributing 133,115 square feet. However, several other submarkets posted losses in absorption. Supply remains tight as Orange County has recorded no new office completions so far this year, and only one project — the 168,137-square-foot building underway at the Anaheim Ducks’ $5 billion mixed-use development — is under construction. The project is expected to deliver in the fourth quarter, and is already 23 percent pre-leased. Office conversions are also removing space from the market. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Taco Bell leases 254,162 SF at Alton HQ, Irvine, Orange County—largest OC office lease in 5 years
HQ relocation from current Irvine location; occupancy in 2028; Orange County vacancy fell to 15.4%
OC office market gained 265,394 SF YTD; q3 avg asking rent $3.02/SF/mo (+$0.12 YoY)
stories.summary: Taco Bell signed a 254,162 SF office lease at Irvine Company's Alton HQ in Orange County—the largest office lease in five years. The company plans to relocate from its current Irvine headquarters in 2028. Orange County's office market tightened in Q3 with vacancy falling to 15.4% (from 17.1% YoY), rents rising to $3.02/SF/month, and positive YTD net absorption of 265,394 SF despite slowing Q3 activity.
stories.impact: Positive but qualified multifamily signal for Irvine/Orange County: Taco Bell's 2028 HQ move and broader office tightening signal corporate confidence and employee headcount stability in OC. However, office strength in Orange County has not reliably translated to apartment demand (tight office market can reflect automation/lower occupancy per SF). Developers should monitor Taco Bell's hiring plans and wage growth post-move; if it drives 1,000+ white-collar jobs, target family/renter-friendly product in Irvine and nearby Tustin/Santa Ana for 2027–2029 delivery.

stories.title: Yves Saint Laurent to Open Store at Kering’s 717 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Luxury French fashion house Yves Saint Laurent will open a new store at 717 Fifth Avenue, a new report revealed. According to a market report released by CBRE, the Kering-owned fashion house, once known as YSL for its founder, the late Yves Saint Laurent, will open in nearly 9,600 square feet in the base of the former Corning Glass Building that sits across East 56th Street from Trump Tower. Saint Laurent is currently at 3 East 57th Street, where it opened in 2003. That store was expanded to 14,071 square feet and renovated in 2015. According to property records, the original lease on East 57th Street ended in 2022 and had no renewal options. Since the fashion retailer is still there, the company likely signed a five-year extension during the pandemic, which would come due in October 2027. The building is managed by Buchbinder & Warren, which did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Kering bought the lower four floors at 717 Fifth Avenue in January 2024 for $963 million from Jeff Sutton’s Wharton Properties and SL Green Realty. The condominium has about 110,000 square feet that encompasses three floors of retail and one office floor. Most of the retail is occupied by Dolce & Gabbana and Armani. In December 2025, facing financial pressure, Kering sold a 60 percent stake to the large French private equity investment firm, Ardian, revaluing the commercial condominium to $900 million at $7,830 per square foot, but giving Kering a $690 million cash boost. It was expected at the time that Kering would begin to bring its own brands under its roof. Along with Saint Laurent, Kering encompasses Gucci, Balenciaga, Bottega Veneta, McQueen, Brioni plus Boucheron, Pomellato, DoDo, Qeelin, Ginori 1735 as well as Kering Eyewear. Gucci is housed across the street in Trump Tower and it is unclear whether they will once again extend that lease of nearly 50,000 square feet, which was renegotiated during COVID-19 with a rent reduction and extension beyond its 2026 en
bullets: Yves Saint Laurent opening at 717 Fifth Avenue, NYC; ~9,600 SF, Kering-owned building
Relocating from 3 East 57th Street (opened 2003, expanded 2015); new lease due Oct 2027
Kering acquired 717 Fifth lower 4 floors for $963M in Jan 2024 from Wharton Properties/SL Green
stories.summary: Yves Saint Laurent will open a new flagship store of approximately 9,600 SF at 717 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, relocating from its current location at 3 East 57th Street (which may see lease renewal in October 2027). Kering, the parent company, acquired the lower four floors of 717 Fifth Avenue in January 2024 for $963 million, signaling luxury brand confidence in Fifth Avenue retail positioning.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily relevance. Luxury retail consolidation on Fifth Avenue reflects Midtown Manhattan property investment but does not signal residential demand or development opportunity for Trammell Crow in the region.

stories.title: Northern Virginia Office Vacancy Falls Again as AI, Defense Demand Builds
stories.excerpt: Northern Virginia’s office market continued to tighten in the third quarter as more demand from artificial intelligence, technology and defense tenants bolstered weaker leasing activity. The market posted 672,378 square feet of positive net absorption during the quarter, reversing losses from the first half of the year tied to buildings being removed from the market, according to JLL. The National Science Foundation’s 380,000-square-foot move to 401 Dulany Street accounted for much of the gain. Northern Virginia’s office vacancy rate fell for a sixth straight quarter to 21.7 percent. Total available space dropped to 33.6 million square feet, its lowest level in a decade, and 25.5 percent below the 45.1 million-square-foot peak in 2023. Leasing activity slowed to just 1.3 million square feet on the quarter, with no deals of more than 100,000 square feet. AI, technology and defense companies committed to more than 300,000 square feet of net new space. And defense spending and tech investment are expected to continue driving momentum. Relocations and new leases have accounted for 58 percent of leasing so far in 2026 in a reverse to the renewal era of 2021 through 2023. Office supply is beginning to strengthen rents, according to JLL. Class A direct asking rents reached $42.51 per square foot per year, while overall direct asking rents averaged $38.13. JLL’s longer-term data shows asking rents have risen since 2022 for Trophy, Class A and Class B properties, while Class C rents have slipped. New construction remains virtually nonexistent, with only about 34,000 square feet underway. Meanwhile, more than 10 million square feet of existing office inventory has been proposed for redevelopment, a dynamic JLL expects will continue tightening the lower end of the market while limited Trophy supply pushes demand toward Class A properties. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Northern Virginia office vacancy fell to 21.7% (Q3, 6th straight quarter decline)
NSF 380K SF move to 401 Dulany Street; AI/tech/defense tenants committed 300K+ SF net new
Total available space 33.6M SF, 25.5% below 2023 peak; leasing slowed to 1.3M SF/quarter
stories.summary: Northern Virginia's office market tightened further in Q3 with vacancy falling to 21.7% (sixth consecutive quarter of decline) and total available space at 33.6 million SF—its lowest in a decade and 25.5% below the 2023 peak. The National Science Foundation's 380,000 SF relocation to 401 Dulany Street and AI/tech/defense sector commitments of 300,000+ SF of net new space drove positive absorption of 672,378 SF, though overall leasing activity slowed.
stories.impact: STRONG positive signal for Northern Virginia multifamily: AI, tech, and defense sector consolidation around Dulany Street (McLean/Reston corridor) signals sustained job growth and white-collar wage expansion. With office vacancy at 21.7% and inventory at decadal lows, multifamily demand will intensify as employers hire and retain talent. Developers should prioritize site acquisition in Reston, McLean, Herndon, and along the Dulany Street/Route 7 corridor for 2027–2029 delivery; competition for sites will accelerate as office scarcity becomes recognized.

stories.title: S3 Capital Supplies $20M for Boutique Miami Beach Condo
stories.excerpt: Trinity Southern has closed on the purchase of a development site and nabbed a $19.5 million construction loan for a boutique condo development on the waterfront in Miami Beach, property records show. S3 Capital provided the financing for the eight-story development, called Twenty Nine Indian Creek, at 2901 Indian Creek Drive in the Mid-Beach neighborhood, near the Miami Beach Edition hotel. In tandem with the financing, the New York-based developer broke ground and purchased the 15,000-square-foot site for $8 million from another New York-based firm, JMH Development, which had initially proposed the condo development. Twenty Nine Indian Creek will house 16 units, totaling 24,842 square feet of sellable space, and a parking garage, according to a filing to Miami-Dade County. So far, 10 units have sold, Dana Lozito, who leads Trinity Southern, told Commercial Observer. Luxury condo developments in Miami Beach, and South Florida more broadly, remain attractive to lenders. Just this week, a Terra-led partnership has secured a $507 million construction loan for a condo tower in South Beach. In an unusual move, the financing from Tyko Capital came even before the sponsors had launched sales. Typically, developments need to hit certain sales benchmarks before securing funding. Last year, Mast Capital and Starwood Capital Group landed $390 million in construction debt for a OMA-designed project in Mid-Beach. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Trinity Southern secures $19.5M construction loan from S3 Capital for 16-unit luxury condo, Miami Beach
Twenty Nine Indian Creek, 2901 Indian Creek Drive Mid-Beach; 24,842 SF, 10 units pre-sold
Site purchased for $8M from JMH Development; 8-story development with parking garage
stories.summary: Trinity Southern closed on an $8 million land purchase and received a $19.5 million construction loan from S3 Capital for Twenty Nine Indian Creek, a boutique 16-unit luxury condo project in Miami Beach's Mid-Beach neighborhood. The project has already sold 10 of 16 units and is now under construction. The transaction reflects strong lender appetite and buyer demand for luxury condo development in Miami Beach and South Florida.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Condo/for-sale development (rather than rentals) operates on different underwriting and exit timelines. However, the deal signals strong capital availability and buyer confidence in Miami Beach waterfront. If condo activity is robust, it may indicate that high-net-worth migration to Miami outpaces supply, potentially signaling unmet demand for luxury rental apartments in similar Miami Beach/Mid-Beach submarkets. Monitor condo absorption; if units sell below listing, it signals soft demand that could weaken rental market; if condo waiting lists form, it signals supply-constrained luxury rental opportunity.
